coverage: Pre-market, Mon Nov 23 (covers Fri Nov 20 close and the weekend)
moodReason: All three major indexes ended the week of Nov 16 to 20 in correction, with the Nasdaq down about 10% on AI valuation fears and a hawkish Fed. Sunday futures bounced, but the trend is still negative.

stories.headline: Tech rout drives the worst week since April 2025 as the Nasdaq falls about 5%
stories.what: The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.3% on Friday Nov 20 and the S&P 500 about 3.7%, with Nvidia down about 10%. For the week the Dow fell about 8%, the S&P 500 about 8.6% and the Nasdaq about 10%, the weakest week since early April 2025. The Dow and S&P 500 entered correction territory on Nov 19.
stories.why: Investors are repricing AI-linked stocks over doubts that AI spending and data center build-outs will produce enough profit to justify valuations. Tech carries a large share of index weight, so the selloff drags the whole market lower.

sources.title: CNBC: S&P 500 and Dow close in correction, Nov 19 2026

stories.headline: Rate-hike odds rise ahead of the Dec 9 Fed meeting under Chair Warsh
stories.what: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has struck a hawkish tone, and a Kalshi snapshot cited in recent coverage gave about 91% odds of a 25 basis point hike at the Dec 9 meeting and about 2% odds of a cut. The fed funds range is 3.75% to 4.00% after the Oct 28 hold.
stories.why: Higher expected rates raise borrowing costs and lower the present value of future earnings, which hits high-valuation growth stocks hardest. The Russell 2000 fell about 2.8% on Nov 20 as small caps, which borrow heavily, sold off.

sources.title: Advisor Perspectives: Kevin Warsh Is Now Free to Unleash His Inner Hawk

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield back above 5% and the dollar at its highest since April 2025
stories.what: The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5% in mid-November for the first time since late October, and the dollar index climbed to near 103.4, its highest since April 2025. Hotter inflation data and hawkish Fed comments drove the move.
stories.why: Higher yields make bonds more competitive with stocks and raise financing costs across the economy. A stronger dollar reduces the dollar value of overseas earnings for US multinationals.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices a record $81 billion IPO, then fades in its Nasdaq debut
stories.what: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on Nov 19 under the ticker ANT after pricing at $83 a share, raising about $81.3 billion in the IPO. The stock opened at $111.50 but slid to the mid-$90s by midday. It is the largest IPO on record, and coverage tied the wider AI selloff to the debut.
stories.why: The fade from the opening price was read as a sign of limits to appetite for AI valuations, which fed the bubble debate. Amazon and Alphabet together hold about 28.4% of Anthropic, so their shares are tied to its price. Anthropic is on track to join the Nasdaq 100 on Dec 21.

stories.headline: US futures rebound on Sunday after the tech rout
stories.what: US equity futures traded higher on Sunday evening Nov 22 to start the shortened week. Reports put S&P 500 futures up roughly 1% to 2% and Nasdaq 100 futures up about 1.9%, after Friday's sell-off.
stories.why: A futures bounce after a sharp drop suggests some dip buying, but it does not settle whether AI valuations and rate expectations have reset. Monday's cash session will show whether the rebound holds.

sources.title: CNBC: S&P 500 futures rebound sharply to rise 2%, Nov 22 2026

stories.headline: Gold and bitcoin lose ground as yields and the dollar rise
stories.what: Gold fell about 4.6% to near $3,880 in mid-November and was reported near $3,735 later in the week. Total crypto market value fell about 20.6% in a month, and bitcoin dropped below $70,000 in a later selloff.
stories.why: Gold pays no interest, so higher yields and a stronger dollar reduce its appeal. Bitcoin has traded more like a risk asset alongside tech, so the AI selloff weighs on it too.

bottomLine: US stocks enter a holiday-shortened week after their weakest stretch since April 2025, led by AI and mega-cap tech. Sunday futures point to some dip buying, but a Fed that now leans toward hikes and a 10-year yield above 5% keep pressure on high valuations. The near-term tests are whether tech holds its bounce into Thanksgiving and how Anthropic trades ahead of the Dec 9 Fed decision.
